news.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
news.body: OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program will work with utilities to help future compute campuses support grid reliability and protect consumer electricity costs.

news.title: Powering up for a pivotal moment
news.body: From a nuclear revival to qubits, the MIT Energy Initiative’s annual research conference tracked deployment of today’s technologies to discovery of tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

news.title: LifeVal
news.body: Introducing LifeVal, a benchmark measuring how well AI helps people complete everyday tasks, from finding childcare to managing finances and government paperwork.

news.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery
news.body: The MIT professors collaborated to identify the first AI-discovered antibiotic, a scientific breakthrough that is widely recognized as a milestone in AI-driven drug discovery.

news.title: Qodo builds context into AI code review with Codex
news.body: Qodo brings company knowledge and coding standards into Codex, helping developers catch P0 issues across repositories before opening a pull request.

news.title: MIT affiliates named 2026 Schmidt Sciences AI2050 Fellows
news.body: Five MIT faculty members and two additional alumni are honored with fellowships to advance research on beneficial AI.

news.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?
news.body: MIT professors Adam Berinsky and Chara Podimata discuss a new project to track how AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

news.title: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences
news.body: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt signal to help website operators communicate their AI training preferences to participating providers.

news.title: Community safety report and new protections for teens
news.body: OpenAI is strengthening violence prevention in ChatGPT with expanded safeguards, earlier interventions, and a new commitment to public safety reporting.

news.title: Fair use benefits everyone
news.body: OpenAI shares excerpts from court briefs by creators, academics, accessibility advocates, and legal experts, among others, on how fair use supports AI training and innovation.

news.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
news.body: OpenAI’s updated Model Spec outlines five core values to guide more capable AI toward sound judgment, human agency, and faithfulness to human intent.

news.title: Granite Switch 4.1.1 — Update models like you update software
How we detect frontier model misalignment
news.body: OpenAI uses layered monitoring to detect frontier model misalignment and unauthorized agent behavior so responders can intervene before incidents escalate.

news.title: How Ropes & Gray is developing AI for transactional diligence
news.body: Ropes & Gray is developing AI for transactional diligence with OpenAI. Lawyers review grouped documents, summaries, and reports before advising clients.

papers.title: Generative Design and Graph Neural Network Screening of Novel Bimetallic Alloy Catalysts for the Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
papers.body: arXiv:2610.41932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying earth-abundant catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a central challenge in scalable green hydrogen production. We present a computational pipeline that couples diffusion-based generative modelling, machine-learning force-field relaxation, and graph neural network (GNN) property prediction to discover bimetallic HER catalysts beyond the structures and stoichiometries covered by existing adsorption databases. A generative model (MatterGen) is fine-tuned on bulk alloy structures labelled with their minimum hydrogen adsorption energy and steered towards adsorption energies near zero. papers.body: arXiv:2607.28000v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Iron (Fe) oxidation is a fundamental phenomenon that is scientifically vital and technologically significant. Despite substantial experimental efforts, accurate atomistic modelling of Fe oxidation remains elusive, which requires a reliable interatomic potential, whose development hinges on a representative first-principles training dataset.
